input: Scheduled ventures brief (prompts/ventures/prompt-1.md): continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production.
task: Deepen (flagship 9) league-schedule-generator: find why spring_2026_chesshouse reads 0.527 in the Swiss replay (NEXT.md)

doc_friction.issue: The open item guessed the ChessHouse cause (pre-entered byes clashing with replay absences); the real cause was a duplicate-name parse bug. Comparing the file's points column with the reader's computed scores found it in one step; a guessed cause in a queue entry can send a run down the wrong path.

deviations.why: No separate docs/reports agent doc: the README section, NEXT.md and eval/swiss-exchange-order.md addendum carry what the next run needs.
deviations.did: Recorded findings in the venture README, NEXT.md and eval files.

writeups: ventures/league-schedule-generator/README.md (section 'Players told apart by "(id)" kept their own results')
notes: Root cause: parseResults treats a trailing '(...)' as a note, and trfNames disambiguates duplicate names as 'Name (id)'. ChessHouse's TRF has five players named '0' (national id column), so wins of '0 (154)' etc. as black were credited to the first '0' (player 114 had 3 points after round 1). Fix: read with the bracket kept first; only strip it as a note when a name fails to match. Replay (eval/swiss-bracketed-names.txt, gbtami/swisspairing 193ad99, --pairing bracket): ChessHouse rounds-2+ recall 0.527 -> 0.975, exact 1 -> 5, rounds read 7 -> 9; six chess-results events 0.893 -> 0.948, exact 15 -> 19; every other event identical. trf.test.mjs: 2 new tests, both fail on the old code. Full venture suite: see PR body.
